title: Local compactness, hyperbolic-swap obstruction, and quantitative angle/depth bridges for Zeta23

claims.statement: Vanishing first-scale defect does not force global mean-square proximity to one fixed lattice phase; a slowly strained lattice has O(1) total defect and Theta(N) best fixed-coset squared displacement.

In the ideal finite-periodic all-on-line rectangular model, small first-scale defect forces random-coset local limits and yields the qualitative 5/108 second-scale exclusion at simple density at most 2/3.
Per-pair isolated depth penalties are not additive for arbitrary interacting indefinite blocks; an exact two-pair hyperbolic-swap model has zero combined c=2 defect.

A combined synthesis Riesz lower bound and a negative-family upper bound imply a principal-angle gap, which lower-bounds the collapsed operator defect by (2 eta - eta^2)||Rsharp||_F^2; the exact angle coefficient is sharp for two lines.

A centered frequency-square weighted trace has an exact additive negative contribution -2 sum n_p delta_p^2 from off-line depth and gives a local conditional mean-square depth bound once a source-side lower estimate is available.

Under the complex-argument r^-2 coefficient decay used by Zeta23, the centered frequency-square finite-section tail scales as O(log T T^{(lambda-1)/2}); it vanishes at lambda=3/4 but the same bound is only O(log T) at lambda=1. For real on-line arguments the endpoint bound is O(log T T^-1/2).

For every placement of one load-two reflection pair and one empty residue in the period-six (1,1,1,1,2,0) clock law, the ideal polyphase determinant is nonzero at positive normalized depth and extends nonvanishingly through the divided-difference limit. At zero depth the squared principal angle is at least 3/38 over all phases and placements; every bounded depth interval has a positive Riesz lower bound by compactness.

For every finite period and every disjoint equal-size pair/vacancy residue sets in the shallow divided-difference model, the missing-residue projection is a square Cauchy matrix with nonzero determinant; every fixed finite shallow polyphase system is nondegenerate.

Critical density and simple density 2/3 do not imply a period-independent shallow principal-angle gap. For period 6m with a pair arc opposite a vacancy arc, the raw missing-residue column-average gap is at most 4m/(36m^2-1), while the smallest squared principal angle has the explicit exponential upper bound [6m^2/(5(1-r)^2)]r^(2m-2), r=sqrt(2-sqrt(3)).

If pair residues admit a bijective vacancy matching of circular radius at most R<P/2, then the raw shallow missing-residue column-average transport gap is at least 3/[(P^2+2)sin^2(pi R/P)], tending to at least 3/(pi^2 R^2) for fixed R. This does not control the fully optimized distance to the whole positive span.

At every positive normalized depth, the finite periodic fiber transforms pairwise to a normalized Vandermonde system with nodes on three distinct circles. Its determinant is P^(-P/2)(2a)^(-k) times the Vandermonde product, so every fixed finite positive-depth fiber is exactly nondegenerate.

For every fixed normalized depth a>=0, a consecutive pair-residue block A of length k<=P/2 and any disjoint equally large vacancy set have smallest squared principal angle at most 24 cosh(a/2)^2 Q_a^2 P^2[log k+2]/[k(P^2-1)], Q_a=tanh(a/2)/a with Q_0=1/2. At k=P/6 this is O_a(log P/P), so no density-only global angle gap exists even at fixed positive depth.

validation.boundary: Deterministic checks validate exact finite formulas, asymptotic scaling and numerical linear algebra only; proof candidates still require isolated independent verification.
